editorial:
Imagine your whole world turning upside down when your spouse suddenly vanishes. You get to see this nightmare play out through the eyes of the Peterson family in this gripping drama. Dean Cain plays Scott Peterson, and he does a great job making you feel uneasy about his character from the start. The movie captures that creepy feeling of a suburban neighborhood where everything looks perfect on the outside, but something dark is happening behind closed doors. It focuses on the heartbreak of a missing pregnant wife and the growing suspicion that the husband isn't telling the truth.

What really works here is how the tension builds as the police start digging into Scott's secret life. The pacing is solid, though it feels like a typical early 2000s TV movie. If you love true crime stories that make you want to yell at the screen, you will really enjoy this one.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing the legal fallout of the case. After a long investigation and a trial that captured the whole country, Scott Peterson is found guilty of murdering Laci and their unborn baby. The final scenes focus on the sadness of the family and the closure they get once the truth comes out. It ends with a heavy feeling, confirming that the husband was the killer all along.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime documentaries and courtroom dramas.
